question.text: Under Section 15T of the SEBI Act, appeals to SAT can be made against orders of which of the following authorities?

answer.text: SEBI, an Adjudicating Officer under the SEBI Act, and IRDA or PFRDA
Only an Adjudicating Officer under the SEBI Act

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 15T of the SEBI Act allows appeals to the Securities Appellate Tribunal (SAT) against orders of SEBI, orders of an Adjudicating Officer under the SEBI Act, and orders of IRDA and PFRDA. The standalone option naming all three categories together is the correct answer. The Trap: Each of the other three options names only one category. Candidates who recognise SEBI as the obvious appellant body often miss that SAT's jurisdiction also covers Adjudicating Officer orders and IRDA/PFRDA orders. Note: SAT's appellate jurisdiction extends beyond SEBI alone — it also covers Adjudicating Officer orders and orders of IRDA and PFRDA, giving SAT a securities-and-financial-sector-wide appellate role.
